How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website
as noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration,
but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be
forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2024  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, October 1, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Vice Mayor Menchaca
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Wu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Harrington

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. SAN GABRIEL VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS UPDATE

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF REVISED MINUTES FOR JULY 16 AND AUGUST 20, 2024,
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS, AND NEW MINUTES OF THE
  SEPTEMBER 17, 2024, REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  To increase efficiencies, staff recommends the approval of revised minutes
  incorporating acknowledgement of written public comments received prior to
  the regular City Council meetings of July 16 and August 20, 2024; and approval
  of new minutes of the regular City Council meeting of September 17, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the following:

  1. Revised Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of July 16, 2024.

  2. Revised Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of August 20, 2024.

  3. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of September 17, 2024.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2024  2
   B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. APPOINTMENT TO THE CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION FOR A TERM SET TO
  EXPIRE ON MAY 31, 2025

  The City solicited applications for a vacant seat on the Civil Service Commission
  with a term ending May 31, 2025. On September 11, 2024, the City received an
  application from former Civil Service Commission Douglas Richter. There is no
  fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council appoint Douglas Richter as a Civil
  Services Commissioner to fill the vacancy, effective immediately, for a term
  expiring on May 31, 2025.

  Alternative Recommendation

  Alternatively, the City Council can choose to direct staff to schedule an interview
  with Douglas Richter before the next regular meeting.

  D. POLICE DEPARTMENT PURCHASE OF AN UNMARKED POLICE VEHICLE IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $62,078.10 UTILIZING AIR QUALITY MANAGEMENT
  DISTRICT (AQMD) FUNDS

  An unmarked administrative police vehicle (2016 Ford Explorer Interceptor) is
  past its useful life as it has over 160,0000 miles and exhibits significant
  mechanical and reliability issues. The unit has been budgeted for replacement

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2024  3
   in Fiscal Year 2024-2025 utilizing AQMD funding. This police unit qualifies as a
  “Clean Air Vehicle” since staff opted to purchase the hybrid variant of the 2025
  Ford Explorer Interceptor. There is no impact to the general fund. AQMD funds
  in the amount of $62,078.10 will be utilized for the replacement of the
  administrative police vehicle. The adopted 2024-2025 budget appropriated
  $70,000 in the Police Department’s Special Project Fund account #124-751-51-
  99-201.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Police Chief to purchase
  the vehicle as listed in the quotation for an amount not to exceed $62,078.10.

  E. PURCHASE OF NEW POLICE ALL-TERRAIN VEHICLE - $16,499.99

  The Police Department is requesting to purchase a 2024 Honda SXS700M4 all-
  terrain vehicle (ATV) in the amount of $16,499.99 for Fiscal Year 2024-2025. The
  funding source for the purchase of this ATV will be provided by the California
  Highway Patrol Cannabis Tax Fund Grant #17920. The impact to the grant
  funding is slightly lower than the budgeted amount of $17,000 in the current
  grant fiscal year. It should also be noted that this vehicle will not be used for
  specific enforcement purposes but still needs to be marked for usage as police
  Driving Under the Influence equipment that can be funded utilizing the
  remaining $500 of the grant funding allotted.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the purchase of one 2024
  Honda SXS700M4 all-terrain vehicle from Mountain Motor Sports utilizing
  Cannabis Tax Fund Grant #17920 funds from account #124-751-57-99-383.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 710 AMENDING THE VALLEY BOULEVARD SPECIFIC
  PLAN RELATING TO GROUND FLOOR OFFICE USE AND ESTABLISHING
  MINIMUM DENSITIES (SPA24-001) – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST
  READING

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2024  4
   The proposed Valley Boulevard Specific Plan Amendment would amend the
  Specific Plan relating to ground floor office use and establish minimum
  densities intended to implement the goals and programs identified in the 2021-
  2029 Housing Element. This item was continued from the September 17, 2024
  City Council meeting to allow staff additional time to address the comments
  provided at the meeting. The Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Adopted Budget includes
  the cost for required legal publication (Account #121-702-00-65-000) and
  codification (Account #121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA). An Initial Study/Negative Declaration (IS/ND) was prepared
  for the 2021-2029 Housing Element, as required by the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA), Public Resources Code (PRC) Section 21000 et seq., the CEQA
  Guidelines, and the City of San Gabriel Local Guidelines for Implementing CEQA.
  The IS/ND considered the policies and programs outlined in the Housing Element.
  The Housing Element establishes objectives, policies, and programs to assist the
  City in achieving state-mandated housing goals. No formal land use changes or
  physical development are proposed at this time and future land use and physical
  development  would  require  separate  environmental  evaluation.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1 . Continue the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 710.

  2 . Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 710 by title only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE VALLEY BOULEVARD
  SPECIFIC PLAN RELATING TO GROUND FLOOR OFFICE USE AND
  ESTABLISHING MINIMUM DENSITIES.

  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting.
  The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

  Other Options For Consideration:

  The action of the City Council may be to approve, approve with modifications,
  or deny the proposed zone text amendment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2024  5
   If the City Council determines that the proposed ordinance or any part of the
  ordinance should be denied, the appropriate motion should be adopted.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. GENERAL FUND PRELIMINARY FINANCIAL RESULTS FOR THE FISCAL YEAR
  ENDING JUNE 30, 2024

  City of San Gabriel’s Fiscal Year 2023-2024 concluded on June 30, 2024.This
  report presents the preliminary financial results for the City’s general fund. The
  presented financial results are unaudited and consist of forecasts and estimates
  made by staff. Audited financial statements for the fiscal year ending June 30,
  2024 will be published by December 31, 2024. There is no fiscal impact related
  to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and file this report.

  B. CONSIDERATION TO SUPPORT PROPOSITION 36: THE HOMELESSNESS,
  DRUG ADDICTION, AND THEFT REDUCTION ACT [RESOLUTION NO. 24-
  54]

  The Homelessness, Drug Addiction, and Theft Reduction Act (Proposition 36)
  was introduced in response to the significant rise in homelessness, drug
  addiction, and theft in California following the passage of Proposition 47 in
  2014, which reduced penalties for drug possession and theft. California voters
  will decide the fate of Proposition 36 on the November 5, 2024 ballot.
  Supporters of Proposition 36 include the League of California Cities, California
  District Attorneys Association, and various California law enforcement officials.
  There is no fiscal impact associated with this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2024  6
   Staff recommends that the City Council discuss and choose whether to support
  the initiative. Should Council wish to support the initiative, Resolution No. 24-
  54 is included for consideration.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, October 15, 2024
  at 6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will
  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF OCTOBER 1, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Wu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:35 P.M.
  on Tuesday, October 1, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive,
  San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Menchaca.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Vice Mayor
  Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Human Resources/Risk
  Management Director Edward Macias, Finance Director
  William Kaholokula, Community Development Director
  Aldo Cervantes, Police Chief Edward Elizalde, Fire
  Division Chief Christopher Eakman, and Assistant City
  Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Wu approved the agenda order.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

I  A. 2024 SAN GABRIEL VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS UPDATE

  Katie Ward, Administrative Services Manager, and Nicholas Ryu, Broadband,
  Coyote, and Energy Programs Manager, made the presentation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Erlinda Romo, resident, thanked the San Gabriel Women's Foundation for an
  upcoming Candidate Forum to be held on October 3, 2024, at 6:30 p.m. at the Padilla
  Room, moderated by the League of Women Voters; and requested that the City or
  individual Council Members post an announcement for the Forum on social media.
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  October 1, 2024
   Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident, commented on the transition of power in Mexico,
  the upcoming San Gabriel City Council Candidate Forum, dissolution of the Human
  Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission, written comments submitted for City
  Council meetings, and propositions for the upcoming General Election.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member

I  Harrington, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4E as presented.

  /Vlotion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF REVISED MINUTES FOR JULY 16 AND AUGUST 20, 2024,
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS, AND NEW MINUTES OF THE SEPTEMBER
  17, 2024, REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  The City Council approved the following:

  1. Revised Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of July 16, 2024.

  2. Revised Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of August 20, 2024.

  3. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of September 17, 2024.

I  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved September 6 and 13, 2024, Material Demands for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  C. APPOINTMENT TO THE CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION FOR A TERM SET TO
  EXPIRE ON MAY 31, 2025

  The City Council appointed Douglas Richter as a Civil Services Commissioner to fill
  the vacancy, effective immediately, for a term expiring on May 31, 2025.

  D. POLICE DEPARTMENT PURCHASE OF AN UNMARKED POLICE VEHICLE IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $62,078.10 UTILIZING AIR QUALITY MANAGEMENT DISTRICT
  (AQMD) FUNDS

  The City Council authorized the Police Chief to purchase the vehicle as listed in the
  quotation for an amount not to exceed $62,078.10.

I  E. PURCHASE OF NEW POLICE ALL-TERRAIN VEHICLE - $16,499.99

  The City Council approved the purchase of one 2024 Honda SXS700M4 all-terrain
  vehicle from Mountain Motor Sports utilizing Cannabis Tax Fund Grant #17920
  funds from account #124-751-57-99-383.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  October 1, 2024
   A. ORDINANCE NO. 710 AMENDING THE VALLEY BOULEVARD SPECIFIC PLAN
  RELATING TO GROUND FLOOR OFFICE USE AND ESTABLISHING MINIMUM
  DENSITIES (SPA24-001) - INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  Mayor Wu opened the public hearing.

  Planning Manager Samantha Tewasart made the staff presentation.

  There was no public comment; therefore, Mayor Wu closed the public hearing.

I  Discussion included that the ordinance reflects Planning Commission
  recommendations and City Council direction from the last City Council meeting;
  second floor uses do not affect the quota for the first floor; and types of services
  that fall under medical office use.

  A motion was made by Council Member Ding, seconded by Vice Mayor Menchaca,
  to:

  1. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 710 by title only: "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Amending
  the Valley Boulevard Specific Plan Relating to Ground Floor Office Use and
  Establishing Minimum Densities."

  2.  Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading and
  adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

I  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. GENERAL FUND PRELIMINARY FINANCIAL RESULTS FOR THE FISCAL VEAR
  EN(?ING JUNE 30, 2024

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included safekeeping revenue is evidence money taken into
  the general fund; there may still be some adjusting journal entries and accruals to
  be recorded that are not expected to have a significant impact; departmental
  vacancy savings and impacts; capital projects and equipment purchases carried
  over to the next fiscal year; strategies in place to diversify the revenue stream; and

I  tax revenue stability.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included that any restricted reserves are relatively small amounts.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to receive and file the report.

  B. CONSIDERATION TO SUPPORT PROPOSITION 36: THE HOMELESSNESS,
  DRUG ADDICTION, AND THEFT REDUCTION ACT [RESOLUTION NO. 24-54]

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  October 1, 2024
   City Manager Lazzaretto made the presentation and Mayor Wu explained his
  reasons for requesting this item to be agendized.

  Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident, expressed disappointment in the inclusion of
  this item on the agenda, and stated her opposition to Proposition (Prop) 36 and
  her support of Prop 35.

  Discussion included the increase of crime since the passage of Prop 47; the need
  for repercussions to deter crime; change in crime reporting statistics; Prop 36

I
  includes rehabilitation; the importance of the City's commitment to protecting its
  residents; residents are most concerned about public safety; underreporting of
  crime since Prop 47; Prop 36's addition of fentanyl to the category of hard drugs;
  public safety affects everyone; a desire to change the first Whereas of the
  resolution to remove "unintended consequences including;" the City's opposition
  to Prop 47; consumers pay for theft; crime causes the perception that our City is
  not safe; and the benefit of treatment-mandated felony provisions in Prop 36.

  A motion was made by Council Member Chan, seconded by Council Member
  Harrington, to adopt Resolution No. 24-54 supporting the Homelessness, Drug
  Addiction, and Theft Reduction Act, as amended to remove "unintended
  consequences including" in the first Whereas.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto commented he was looking forward to seeing everyone at
  the Dumpling and Beer Fest on October 4, 2024.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Chan reported on his attendance at a monthly Tri-City Chamber of
  Commerce event and Asian Youth Center annual dinner and award ceremony, and
  expressed his hope to see everyone at the annual Dumping and Beer Fest on October
  4, 2024, from 6:00 - 10:00 P.M.

  Council Member Ding reported on his attendance at the Chinatown Service Center
  53 rd Gala, a Chinese American Insurance Finance Professional Association event, South
  Pasadena Lions Club event, Asian Youth Center 35 th Anniversary Gala, and San Gabriel
  Valley Council of Governments homeless round table; and invited all to the Dumpling

I  and Beer Fest.

  Vice Mayor Menchaca shared her experience as a lunchtime mentor for Senator Susan
  Rubia's Women Inspiring the Next Generation of Sisterhood (WINGS) program; and in
  conjunction with Community Services Director Perez announced upcoming movie
  screenings of Dealing with Dad, which deals with intergenerational trauma, and
  Fragmented, which deals with late-stage dementia.

  Mayor Wu reported on his attendance at Southern California Edison's L.A. leaders'
  round table conference, San Gabriel Historical Association fund-raising dinner, and a
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  October 1, 2024
   Chinese American Elected Official group tour of the Ontario International Airport
  where he discussed collaboration on tourism for the 2028 Olympics.

  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:07 P.M.

I  Respectfully submitted:

  ,?

  SHARON F. CLARK, Chief City Clerk

  Approved this 15th day of October, 2024:

I

I

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 5  October 1, 2024
